result:
Both solutions reach the same answer, p^n + p − 1, using the same three subgroups: orders p−1, p^{n−1}, and p^{n−1}(p−1). I checked the arithmetic and it is correct: p^{n−1}(p−1) + p^{n−1} + (p−1) = p^n + p − 1. Aut(G) is cyclic of order p^{n−1}(p−1), so each divisor corresponds to a unique subgroup, and Solution A states this explicitly.

Neither solution justifies why these three subgroups are the ones that give almost commutative Terwilliger algebras. I could not verify that classification from memory, so the correctness of the answer depends on that unverified step, and it applies equally to both. Solution A's explicit naming of the subgroups is slightly more informative, so I give it a marginal edge.

WINNER: A
